title: A Merciful and Faithful High Priest
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Jesus' faithfulness became our forgiveness. Even when we are faithless, he remains faithful, and he guards us against the evil one.
exhortation: This morning I want to take a minute to dwell on the faithfulness and goodness of God toward us.

Jesus had to become what we could not. We couldn't be faithful the way he was. We needed a faithful high priest, and Aaron and all the priests before Jesus were not enough. But Jesus was perfectly faithful, the exact sacrifice required for the forgiveness of our sins. His faithfulness became our forgiveness.

2 Timothy 2:13 says, "If we are faithless, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself." Jesus knows you. He knows me. He knows the worst parts of us, and he remains faithful toward us. How good is Jesus?

And 2 Thessalonians 3:3 says, "But the Lord is faithful. He will establish you and guard you against the evil one." The Lord protects you. He is with you and has not left you alone. He fights for you against the evil one, and he sends his Spirit to give you power for the gospel mission he has called you to. He never calls you to something he won't be with you in. He is faithful to help you. We serve a faithful, gracious and merciful God. Let's remember that this morning as we worship.
prayer: Lord, we are so grateful that you are faithful. You became human like us, and yet you are so unlike us. You are perfectly faithful and completely loving toward us. We tend to doubt you and think you're like us: that you will fail, get angry, give up or cast us off. But that's not who you are. You are faithful. Thank you that we can put our full trust in you today.

Whatever lies ahead of us, the worry and anxiety, the frustration and anger that rise up, help us run to you, who are faithful and just, who meet us in our need and never leave our side. Help us look to you today and trust in your faithfulness toward us. In Jesus' name, amen.
